agent.problem: Saying “that line again” uses Proverbs 10:8 as well as Proverbs 10:10, since the earlier line is “foolish lips will come to ruin” in verse 8. The card's citation of only Proverbs 10:10 is narrower than the verses it uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

agent.problem: The card explicitly compares Proverbs 10:11 with Proverbs 10:6 when it says the second half is “word for word from verse 6,” but its citation covers only verse 11. It should run from verse 6, the first verse used, through verse 11.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

agent.problem: The wrong answer “How hard each one works” is something Solomon compares elsewhere in this passage: Proverbs 10:4 contrasts idle hands with diligent hands. It is therefore not false anywhere in the passage.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

human.problem: Several story cards state proverbs in the exact BSB wording but without quotation marks, and often without saying Solomon is the speaker. In this card, "A wise heart will receive commandments, but foolish lips will come to ruin. And he who walks in integrity walks securely." reads as Papa Dorin's own statement. The same happens in Stop 1 cards 6, 13, 16 and 18, and Stop 2 cards 9, 16 and 18.
human.question: When a story card uses the exact BSB wording, must it go in quotation marks and be attributed to the speaker, or may Papa Dorin say it unquoted as his own narration?
